inputRequirement: Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall record that a Polar Water Operational Manual is present.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall record that its bridge wings are enclosed.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall have at least two echo-sounding devices.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall have exactly one construction date encoded as xsd:date.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall have a length overall of at least 70 metres.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall record at least 1,200 kilowatts of maximum continuous rating power, using the canonical kilowatt unit.
Synthetic rule: Every ship component in this example shall link to exactly one benchmark entity through connectedToEmergencyPower.
Synthetic rule: Every hull structure in this example shall identify at least one structural connection as an IRI referring to a benchmark entity.
Synthetic rule: A ship in this example shall use Category A or Category B as its controlled polar ship category.
Synthetic rule: A ship in this example shall use IA Super, IA, or IB as its controlled Finnish-Swedish ice class.
Synthetic rule: Each ship component in this example shall have an approved material approval status.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall link to one Polar Ship Certificate Form evidence node with a source and Approved lifecycle state.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall have one timestamped SOSA observation of its working liquid, with a string result.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall provide at least two timestamped daily-low-temperature observations, each recorded as a QUDT degree-Celsius quantity.
Synthetic rule: Every watertight or weathertight closing device in this example shall have a successful winter-clothing operability test status.
Synthetic rule: Every ship in this example shall link to one approved model-test evidence node that identifies its source record.
Synthetic rule: For each ship in this example, persons on board shall not exceed the available survival-equipment capacity.
Synthetic rule: For each ship in this example, personsCapacityRequirement shall equal personsOnBoard plus additionalEquipmentCapacityRequirement.
Synthetic rule: Each ship shall declare whether it operates in polar waters. If it does, the ship shall record that a Polar Water Operational Manual is present.
Synthetic rule: Each ship in this example shall be Category A or B, have a construction date on or after 1 January 2020, have enclosed bridge wings, and have a length overall of at least 60 metres.

Synthetic rule: Where compliance depends on an engineering calculation that is outside the supported direct arithmetic subset, the ship shall provide a calculation case with documented calculation-input evidence and documented calculation-result evidence. The SHACL shape shall verify readiness and evidence only and shall not reconstruct the external numerical method.

Synthetic rule: A nonlinear engineering analysis is performed externally. Every applicable calculation case shall contain acceptance evidence, and the record shall confirm that the resulting permanent deformation assessment is satisfied. The SHACL shape shall not reproduce the nonlinear calculation.
